root_cause: Off-by-one in the loop bound: `for (size_t i = 0; i + 1 < n; i++)` stops before the last element, so a key that occurs ONLY at a[n-1] is never found. CBMC reports a violation of the harness assertion `rc == 1` (behavior found) with e.g. n = 1, a[0] == key (find_first returns 0). Frama-C/WP agrees from the other side: the post-condition `\result == 1` of behavior found cannot be proved (the loop invariants only cover a[0..i) and the loop exits at i == n - 1).
rationale: Iterate over the whole range: `i < n`. With the same invariants (0 <= i <= n; no a[k] == key for k < i) the loop exits with i == n, so 'not found' really means that no element equals key, and an early return happens at the first matching index. *pos is still written only when the key is found. i < n <= SIZE_MAX, so i++ cannot wrap.
